habitat: Singly or in pairs in broad-leaved woodland, mixed bushveld and riverine forest. It fans and pumps its tail while moving through the middle layer.
summary: An uncommon resident. Told from Ashy Flycatcher by its behaviour and white outer tail feathers. The call is a loud teee-reee, and at close range a trill. The Kemp name Fantailed Flycatcher and the code VB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Ashy Flycatcher has no white in the tail and is mostly silent.

viewNotes.note: White outer tail feathers. It fans and pumps the tail.

calls.description: A loud 'teee-reee', the second syllable lower, and a close trill 'wir-ri-rit'. The grade A call is from Hoedspruit. The filename is XC1023579-Tit-Flycatcher_Grey_NdlovumziHoedspruit_20250722_NR14.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it an uncommon resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The body colour is not named. The grade A call is from Hoedspruit. The Kemp name Fantailed Flycatcher and the code VB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^13=8192 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 4096–16384.
